name: Museum of Fine Arts
customer: Art people, students, rainy day crowds
unique: A encyclopedic collection with the country's deepest holdings of Japanese prints, a whole Egyptian tomb chapel and Sargent's murals in the rotunda.
buzz: The Americas wing and the Impressionists are the usual route; the free hour at the end of the day is the local trick.

name: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum
customer: Art people, garden lovers, mystery readers
unique: A Venetian palace built around a flowering courtyard, with paintings hung where the founder left them and empty frames where the 1990 theft took thirteen works.
buzz: The courtyard is the first thing people mention and the empty frames the second; the new wing café is the quiet lunch.

name: Walden Pond
unique: The pond where Thoreau built his cabin, with a replica of the house, a trail around the shore and a beach where people still swim in water clear enough to see the bottom.
buzz: Go early in summer or the lot closes; the cabin site is a half mile walk and the far shore is quiet even on hot days.

name: Harvard Museum of Natural History
unique: The Blaschka glass flowers, 4,300 models made of glass in the 1880s so accurate that botanists still use them, plus a whale skeleton ceiling and a mineral gallery.
buzz: People come for the glass flowers and are surprised by the zoology galleries; the whole museum takes two hours and is good in any weather.

name: Adams National Historical Park
unique: Two presidential birthplaces and the mansion where four generations of Adamses lived, toured by trolley with a ranger who knows the family letters.
buzz: The trolley between the houses is part of the ticket and the library is the quiet highlight; the tour is ranger led and sells out in summer.

name: Blue Hills Reservation
unique: Seven thousand acres of rocky hills inside the Boston beltway, with a 635 foot summit tower, a ski area and trails that feel like New Hampshire.
buzz: The Skyline Trail is the real hike and takes most of a day; locals go on weekday evenings and the summit is a 30 minute climb from the reservation lot.

name: Peabody Essex Museum
customer: Art people, maritime history fans, families
unique: The oldest continuously operating museum in the country, with a Qing dynasty house moved from China, maritime paintings and a Yin Yu Tang courtyard you walk through.
buzz: The Chinese house is the reason people stay an extra hour; the maritime galleries are quieter than the witch museums down the street.

name: Crane Beach
unique: Four miles of barrier beach backed by dunes and a salt marsh, with a greenhead-free ocean side and a trail through the marsh to Ipswich Bay.
buzz: The parking fee is steep and the beach is worth it; the marsh trail at low tide is the quiet alternative when the lot fills.

name: Edaville Family Theme Park
customer: Families with small children, train people
unique: A narrow gauge railroad built to run through cranberry bogs, with a steam engine, a holiday lights season and rides scaled for children under ten.
buzz: The Christmas lights train is the tradition and the summer crowd is thin; parents say one visit a year is enough for older children.

name: Plymouth Long Beach
unique: A three mile sand spit that looks back at Plymouth's waterfront and out to the Gurnet lighthouse, with warm shallow water on the bay side.
buzz: Locals park at the town lot and walk on; the tip at the Gurnet is the walk and the beach is quieter than the Cape.

name: Cape Cod Rail Trail
unique: Twenty two paved miles of old railroad through cranberry bogs, cedar swamp and Cape villages, with bike rentals and a rail trail that reaches the National Seashore.
buzz: The Nickerson State Park stretch is the prettiest and the grade is gentle; rent at Dennis or Orleans and ride one way.

name: Cape Cod Potato Chip Factory Tour
unique: A self guided window tour over the fryers where small batches of kettle chips are cooked, with a sample bag at the end and the smell through the parking lot.
buzz: It is 15 minutes of windows and worth it with children; the shop sells flavors that never leave New England.

name: MASS MoCA
unique: A 19th century textile mill turned into the largest contemporary art museum in the country, with whole buildings given to single artists and a football field of light installations.
buzz: The Sol LeWitt wall drawings and the James Turrell rooms are the pilgrimage; some galleries are the size of a warehouse and the map matters.

name: Clark Art Institute
unique: A small jewel of a museum with 30 Renoirs, a Winslow Homer room and a reflecting pool by Tadao Ando set in 140 acres of meadow and trail.
buzz: People call it the perfect size for two hours; the Ando pools and the walk up Stone Hill are as memorable as the galleries.

name: Hancock Shaker Village
unique: A round stone barn and 20 Shaker buildings where a utopian community lived and worked, with gardens, a working farm and demonstrations of the furniture that shaped modern design.
buzz: The round barn is the architectural highlight and the craft demos are the reason to check the daily schedule; the village is bigger than it looks.

name: Eric Carle Museum of Picture Book Art
unique: The only museum in the country devoted to picture book art, founded by the author of The Very Hungry Caterpillar, with a gallery of original illustrations and a studio where children paint.
buzz: Adults without children love it as much as the children do; the studio and the reading library make it a two hour stop.

name: Smith College Museum of Art
unique: A college museum with a Degas, a Mondrian and a room of African textiles, free to the public and small enough to see before lunch.
buzz: Locals treat it as a free hour; the contemporary galleries rotate often and the print room is open by appointment.

name: Historic Deerfield
customer: History people, decorative arts fans, families
unique: A mile long street of 18th century houses from the 1704 raid, furnished with the chairs and textiles of the Connecticut valley, with a working farm and a tavern.
buzz: The guided house tours are the only way in and the decorative arts collection is serious; the street itself is free to walk.

name: Bridge of Flowers
unique: A 1908 trolley bridge planted end to end with flowers after the trolley stopped running, crossing the Deerfield River above glacial potholes.
buzz: The potholes below are as good as the bridge and both are free; peak bloom is July and the village has a glassblowing studio.

name: Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame
company: Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame
unique: Three floors of basketball history where you can shoot on a court, compare your hand to Shaq's and see the peach basket that started the game in Springfield in 1891.
buzz: The interactive court is what children remember and the enshrinement gallery is for fans; allow two hours and go on a weekday.

name: Springfield Armory National Historic Site
customer: Engineering people, military history fans, families
unique: The armory that made the rifles for every American war from 1794 to 1968, with a room of 1,000 muskets arranged like a pipe organ and the machine tools that invented interchangeable parts.
buzz: The gun collection is the show and the manufacturing story is the real history; rangers explain the machinery and the museum is free.

name: Dr. Seuss National Memorial Sculpture Garden
unique: Bronze Lorax, Horton and Cat in the Hat statues in a courtyard in Theodor Geisel's hometown, with a seated Geisel at his drawing board.
buzz: A free 20 minute stop that photographs well; the museum next door has the original drawings and is the paid companion.

name: Old Sturbridge Village
unique: Two hundred acres of a New England town rebuilt around a common, with a working farm, a tin shop, a printing office and interpreters who stay in character.
buzz: Allow four hours and check the daily schedule for the blacksmith and the farm; children like the animals and the stagecoach.

name: Worcester Art Museum
unique: A small encyclopedic museum with a Roman mosaic floor, the Higgins armor collection and an early Monet, in a 1898 building that is easy to see in two hours.
buzz: The armor and the mosaic are the surprises; locals go on the free first Sunday and the café is good.

name: Purgatory Chasm
unique: A quarter mile granite chasm with walls 70 feet high that you scramble through on boulders, formed by glacial meltwater and a popular local rite of passage.
buzz: The chasm floor is a boulder hop and not for sandals; the rim trail is the easy version and the park is free.

name: Aquinnah Cliffs
unique: Colored clay cliffs on the western tip of Martha's Vineyard, tribal land above a beach of red and white sand, with a lighthouse and a view to the Elizabeth Islands.
buzz: The cliffs are protected and you cannot climb them; the beach walk at low tide is the way and the sunset from the overlook is the photo.

name: Menemsha
customer: Harbor people, sunset chasers, seafood eaters
unique: A working fishing harbor on Martha's Vineyard where the catch is sold off the boat, the beach faces west and the sunset is a nightly event with people applauding.
buzz: Buy chowder and lobster from the shack and eat on the bulkhead; parking in the village is tight and the beach lot closes at sunset time.

name: New Bedford Whaling Museum
unique: The world's largest whaling museum, with half scale whale skeletons hanging over a full scale whaling ship, a scrimshaw collection and the logbooks of the voyages that made the city rich.
buzz: The skeleton room is the one people describe; the museum does not soften the industry and the harbor walk outside completes it.

name: Battleship Cove
unique: The most decorated American battleship of the Second World War, the USS Massachusetts, plus a destroyer and a submarine you can walk through, all tied up together.
buzz: Children can sleep on board with scout groups; the submarine is tight and the battleship guns are the photo.

name: Lizzie Borden House
customer: True crime people, history fans, ghost hunters
unique: The 1892 house where the Borden murders happened, now a bed and breakfast, with a tour that walks the rooms and lays out the evidence.
buzz: Guides present the case without pretending to solve it; overnight guests report things and the tour is more history than haunt.

name: Nantucket Whaling Museum
unique: A candle factory turned museum with a 46 foot sperm whale skeleton on the roof, a restored 1840s whaleship hold and the story of the island that lit America.
buzz: The roof walk with the skeleton and harbor view is the highlight; the museum is the best rainy day on the island.

name: Cisco Brewers
unique: A brewery, winery and distillery in a gray shingled barn outside town, with picnic tables, oyster shucking and live music on summer afternoons.
buzz: The outdoor scene is the point and the island prices are real; go early, the tasting room fills after three.
